episodes.213085: Scattered thunderstorms produced localized wind damage, localized flooding and one brief tornado during the afternoon and evening of June 24th.
episodes.213086: Scattered thunderstorms produced isolated wind damage and isolated flooding during the evening of June 24th.
episodes.213156: The season's first rendition of the North American Monsoon high developed over south-central and southwestern NM with increased low-level moisture intruding beneath it. Faster westerly flow along the northern periphery of the high allowed for some convective organization and stronger afternoon thunderstorms. Relatively warm conditions and low humidity also allowed for strong downdrafts to occur yielding severe wind gusts from decaying thunderstorms mainly over western and central NM each day. Several of these dry downbursts produced blowing dust with one particular event resulting in zero visibility in Rio Rancho on the 25th. Storms through central and eastern NM were wetter in nature threatening locally heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported in Raton on the 24th, with another report of heavy rains producing a landslide from steep terrain near Jemez Springs along NM Highway 4 on the 26th. Other storms produced various severe wind gusts and hail across portions of northern and central NM each day.
episodes.213187: Several rounds of thunderstorms occurred during the period of June 25th and June 27th as a frontal boundary remained near the area. Some areas received 3-6 inches of rainfall over a short period of time. Thunderstorms produced a few tornadoes on the evening of June 26th.
episodes.213328: Moist upslope low level flow and hot temperatures allowed thunderstorms to develop on the higher terrain of eastern New Mexico on the afternoon of the 24th. This thunderstorm activity consolidated into several loosely organized segments as they moved into West Texas. The strongest storms remained anchored to a remnant surface boundary draped across the southern Texas Panhandle. These storms were able to produce widespread severe wind gusts across the extreme southern Texas Panhandle due to a very dry sub-cloud layer.
episodes.213692: Thunderstorms developed over central and southern Wyoming and became severe late in the afternoon through the late evening hours of June 24th. Large hail and strong gusty winds were reported.
episodes.213693: A QLCS moved quickly across central and southeast Wyoming during the middle afternoon to late afternoon hours. Most strong gusty winds were reported with a few severe hail reports. Thunderstorm wind damage was reported near Cheyenne, including a derailed train with shipping containers near Interstate 25.
episodes.213814: High pressure over New Mexico helped trigger new storms off the higher terrain. These storms then moved to the south and east into the combined Panhandles. With favorable instability and wind shear, these storms became strong to severe with the main hazards being large hail and damaging winds. There were some supercells that did produce tornadoes across portions of the eastern combined Panhandles as well as high end wind damage from straight line winds. Given sufficient moisture in place, slow moving storms or storms that moved over the same locations, a few communities in the eastern combined Panhandles did receive heavy rainfall that resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.213837: High pressure over New Mexico helped trigger new storms off the higher terrain. These storms then moved to the south and east into the combined Panhandles. With favorable instability and wind shear, these storms became strong to severe with the main hazards being large hail and damaging winds. There were some supercells that did produce tornadoes across portions of the eastern combined Panhandles as well as high end wind damage from straight line winds. Given sufficient moisture in place, slow moving storms or storms that moved over the same locations, a few communities in the eastern combined Panhandles did receive heavy rainfall that resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.213896: An upper-level trough moving across the Great Lakes brought ample lift to portions of northern Pennsylvania that lead to thunderstorm development during the afternoon and evening hours of June 25, 2026. A narrow corridor of sufficient instability (1000 J/kg) and bulk shear (30 knots) allowed for marginally severe thunderstorms to form across western Pennsylvania. As these storms developed, upscale growth continued into portions of Clearfield and Centre counties, where a severe thunderstorm brought multiple instances of tree damage south of Clearfield. This appears to have occurred when the thunderstorm's core dropped towards the surface as radar analysis outlined that the storm rapidly weakened further east throughout the evening hours.
episodes.213990: Thunderstorms developed into portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the early morning hours of the 25th, near a warm front that stretched across the area. Locally heavy rainfall resulted in isolated flash flooding. Another round of thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon hours, near a remnant outflow boundary from the earlier thunderstorms. These thunderstorms moved southeast and produced large hail up to quarter size and damaging wind.
episodes.214019: A cold frontal boundary progressed across the southeastern states on the 23rd of June before slowing progress and nearly stalling over the northeast FL/southeast GA region. Plenty of summer moisture and instability in the vicinity of the boundary resulted in numerous to widespread showers and thunderstorms for several days in a row.
episodes.214098: Very hot temperatures and convergence within a surface trough allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop late in the afternoon on the 25th. The hot temperatures allowed storms to be high based producing mostly severe wind gusts. One of the more robust updrafts produced quarter size hail in the city of Lubbock. The most impressive storm of the evening was one that tracked near Slaton (Lubbock County). This storm generated a microburst with a peak wind gust of 110 mph measured by the Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet. A storm survey the next day revealed very localized damage around the mesonet site northeast of Slaton. Cotton crops were destroyed and mesquite trees were stripped. Additionally, irrigation pivots were damaged and partially rolled. A heavy gate damaged the fence surrounding the mesonet site but no damage to the sensors occurred. Later in the evening, a line of thunderstorms developed on an outflow boundary moving into the northwestern South Plains. These thunderstorms continued to produce intermittent severe wind gusts as they tracked across the northern South Plains into the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle.
episodes.214149: A disturbance rounding the top of an upper-level ridge along with a nearby stationary boundary resulted in shower and thunderstorm development mainly across portions of southeast New Mexico. One storm managed to produce a severe wind gust at the Tatum Mesonet.
episodes.214151: Disturbances in the upper-level flow, coupled with upslope flow in the higher terrain, caused shower and thunderstorm development across west Texas and southeast New Mexico. Dry low-levels allowed several storms to produce strong downbursts, the strongest of which occurred in Seagraves, where damage to multiple buildings was reported.
episodes.214200: Thunderstorms produced large hail up to golf ball size across St. Clair County, with small hail reported in a few other counties. Thunderstorm winds also blew down trees in Marysville.
episodes.214356: Several severe thunderstorms impacted portions of western Oklahoma on the evening and night of the 25th. An initial supercell thunderstorm (previously tornadic across Beaver County, Oklahoma) moved into northwestern Oklahoma and produced hail and severe winds. Additional thunderstorm activity moved eastward off of a dryline across the eastern Texas Panhandle, producing occasional reports of large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.214470: Clusters of strong thunderstorms along the coast produced a few measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.214489: Numerous thunderstorms tracked across eastern Colorado during the late afternoon and evening hours of the 24th. Hail, strong winds, and two tornadoes were observed. In addition heavy rainfall in the Evergreen area produced flash flooding late on the 24th and early on the 25th.
episodes.214610: A stationary front draped along the coast of Louisiana served as a focus for thunderstorm development.  As the thunderstorms developed, several waterspouts formed over the coastal waters just offshore of coastal Louisiana.
episodes.214661: A typical summertime pattern produced scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms with occasional severe weather reported.
episodes.214680: A stationary front draped across Arkansas in tandem with an approaching upper level trough axis would spur multiple days of severe winds, flash flooding, and heavy rain totals for the multi-day event across the state of Arkansas.
episodes.215003: Scattered thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts across Lake Erie.
episodes.215005: Severe thunderstorms produced reports of damaging winds and large hail across northern Ohio.
episodes.215236: Severe storms moved across portions of central MS during the afternoon hours of June 25 2026 producing damaging wind gusts and a few down trees.
episodes.215306: Thunderstorms developed over northeastern Colorado and the southern Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon and early evening hours of June 24th. As activity moved to the east and southeast, storms became severe with strong winds and large hail. Hail up to the size of baseballs was reported near Wauneta and wind gusts up to 77 MPH were reported near Grant. Thunderstorm wind damage, with winds estimated at 80 MPH overturned multiple pivots and damaged buildings south of Madrid.
episodes.215327: Late day and evening thunderstorms becoming strong in portions of central Wyoming. To the southwest of Cody, nickel sized hail was reported. In Riverton, a strong thunderstorms produced large amounts of hail up to penny size that accumulated a few inches in some locations. Very heavy rain accompanied the hail, with a retired National Weather Service meteorologist reporting 1.40 inches of rain and melted hail in only 30 minutes. As a result, there were numerous reports of minor street flooding and some flooded basements.
episodes.215328: Another shortwave crossed Wyoming and brought another round of strong to severe thunderstorms, primarily impacting Natrona County but also portions of Fremont and Park County. A line of thunderstorms moved through Fremont and Natrona Counties bringing high wind. The highest wind gust reported was 67 mph at Scenic Drive on the south side of Casper. In northern Natrona County, quarter sized hail was reported to south of Midwest. In Park County, there was a report of nickel size hail to the southeast of Cody. North of Jeffrey City, there was a brief QLCS tornado. The tornado remained over open country and caused no known damage.
episodes.215334: On the afternoon of June 25, scattered thunderstorms developed and produced occasional wind damage and at least one report of hail. With storms tracking slowly over the same areas, heavy rain also led to flash flooding.
episodes.215536: Several supercell thunderstorms developed within the warm sector of a broad surface low over central Wisconsin. The clusters of storms tracked southeastward through south central Wisconsin during the afternoon and early evening. Sporadic wind damage to trees and power lines occurred including hail around one inch in diameter.
episodes.215558: Broad forcing for ascent in the left exit region of a 60 knot mid-level jet allowed for scattered thunderstorms in an environment with upper 70s temperatures and low 60s dew points. A sufficiently unstable airmass with 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE and 40-60 knots of effective shear beneath the core of the jet supported some storm organization with an all hazards day in discrete cells.
episodes.215559: Broad forcing for ascent in the left exit region of a 60 knot mid-level jet allowed for scattered thunderstorms in an environment with upper 70s temperatures and low 60s dew points. A sufficiently unstable airmass with 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE and 40-60 knots of effective shear beneath the core of the jet supported some storm organization with an all hazards day in discrete cells.
episodes.215561: A strengthening Pacific trough and well timed shortwave combined with sufficient instability and marginal shear to result in numerous showers and thunderstorms across the region. Most were sub-severe, but two managed to strengthen enough to result in reports of severe hail.
episodes.215606: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rainfall to Benson, AZ causing flash flooding. A trained spotter reported water from curb to curb with an estimated 6 inches of water on roadways.
episodes.215623: During the late evening hours on the 24th, a thunderstorm complex moved into Yuma County from the northwest, producing a measured 62 mph wind gust southwest of Vernon.
episodes.215728: An approaching cold front triggered clusters of strong thunderstorms across northern Illinois during the late afternoon and evening of June 24th.  One of the southernmost storms tracked across Woodford County, resulting in 60mph wind gusts and minor urban flooding.
episodes.215734: Weakly sheared, moderately unstable environment of deep layer supported early afternoon thunderstorms that produced wind damage near Bronson in Levy County.
episodes.215756: Persistent enhanced westerly flow with multiple embedded shortwave troughs brought multiple instances of severe wind gusts and hail to northern Utah as well as flash flooding to Sevier county.
episodes.215921: A thunderstorm produced a strong wind gust in Vero Beach.
episodes.215973: Multiple rounds of storms occurred June 26-28th, 2026 resulting in significant flash flooding over southern Indiana and central Kentucky as well as an EF-0 tornado.  Several flash flood warnings were issued over the 2 day period with Considerable Flash Flooding in multiple locations and even Flash Flood Emergencies in some areas. Rainfall totals for the weekend ended up in an area wide 2-4 inches with swaths of 6-10+ inches!!  Unfortunately 3 fatalities were confirmed due to flooding in Madison County, KY, and 1 fatality indirectly related to the flooding occurred on Floyds Fork in Jefferson County, KY.
episodes.215978: An early morning thunderstorms had lighting strike a tree downing it damaging a neighboring house.

This is the first tornado this storm produced as it intensified. The tornado condensed briefly multiple times along this path. The track was estimated using eye witness reports, pictures, and|videos together with radar data. Most of the tornado path was estimated by triangulating the location using chaser video/pictures and utilizing radar data. Toward the end of the life cycle of the tornado, after becoming rain wrapped and weakening, the tornado did encounter some damage indicators. Damage included large tree limbs which were snapped and one uprooted tree, all of which were around an old dilapidated homestead. Adjacent power lines were not damaged and this also provided clues to the intensity toward the end of the life-cycle. Radar imagery and video suggests the tornado was potentially stronger earlier in the track while in open grasslands. Maximum width was also estimated using photos and video. The maximum estimated wind speeds were 85mph.

A damage path was discovered across northern Wheeler County associated with a supercell circulation suggesting a weak tornado. In addition, a storm chaser documented a periodic funnel with the storm and although they didn't fully condense to the ground, there was periodic dust picked up at the surface. Isolated damage indicators provided challenges for the survey, however a relatively narrow path of damage mainly consisted of snapped large tree limb existed from west to southwest of Allison. There was one small outbuilding destroyed as well, but the EF1 tornado rating was based on snapped power poles early in the track. Otherwise, most of the path was|EF0 damage. The maximum estimated wind speed was 90mph.
